The Woodfibre LNG Project is located approximately 7 km west-southwest of Squamish, British Columbia. It involves the construction and operation of a liquefied natural gas (LNG) export facility on the previous Woodfibre pulp mill site, which would have a storage capacity of 250,000 m3 and would produce approximately 2.1 million tons per year of LNG.
 Woodfibre Management Ltd. is a privately held Canadian company based in Vancouver and a subsidiary of Pacific Energy Corporation Limited.
 Position 
 The Supply Chain Manager   is an integral part of Woodfibre LNG ’s dynamic team. You will be responsible to execute all procurement and contracting management support for the Company. This includes strategic sourcing, pre-qualification of local suppliers and subcontractors, preparation of tender packages and evaluation reports, managing shipping logistics, warehousing, management of changes, claims etc. This position is based in Vancouver, with some travel to the Squamish site as required. The successful candidate reports directly to the Head of Procurement and Supply Chain and will act as a Subject Matter Expert in the implementation of the   SAP implementation at Woodfibre. The role will play an essential part in supporting the company transition from the construction phase into the start-up and operations phases of the project.
 Key Responsibilities : 
 The successful applicant will:
 Be a key member of the WLNG Procurement team, responsible for procurement, contracting, warehousing, subcontract requirements, and LNG Operations requirements.
 Provide strategic support and insights to Head of Procurement & SCM on executive reporting for better business decision making. Identify contract spend consolidation opportunities, increase company bargain power on the market, and optimize internal procurement processes / cost-effectiveness.
 Steward the end-to-end Contracting and Procurement processes for Woodfibre LNG, encompassing sourcing, purchasing, shipping, and warehousing activities.  
 Manage strategic sourcing and supplier qualification, optimizing sourcing strategies and maintaining relationships with suppliers.
 Procure goods and services for the Business Units in line with budget and business plan.
 Manage Procure to Pay end to end process to ensure competitiveness and compliance (with the company’s regulations and all Squamish Nation bidding requirements and fully support the application of the Impact Benefit Agreements).
 Manage contract administration and supplier performance to ensure contractors fulfilling contractual obligations.
 Prepare regular reports on the status of contracts, shipments, and warehousing activities, providing insights into procurement and logistics operations.
 Resolve contract payment and compliance disputes where needed.
 Implement and interpret the company’s policies and procedures correctly; develop, recommend and coordinate the implementation of continuous improvement projects related to Contracting and Procurement.
 Support the implementation of company’s procurement processes in SAP and support the roll-out of SAP-Procurement in the company     
 Required Experience : 
 Bachelor’s degree in business, accounting & finance, engineering or a related field from an accredited university.
 10 + years’ experience in contracts management and procurement, preferably in oil & gas with strong knowledge of contracting procurement for operation
 5+ years of experience in managing contracts and familiar with contract laws with the ability to draft, amend or revise contract clauses confidently and appropriately.
 Hands-on experience in SAP or other ERP systems.
 Proven ability to work with multiple business units, including, operations and other end users to ensure the scope of work is accurate and complete.
 Excellent negotiation techniques with strong can-do attitude and owner mentality.
 Extensive experience working in matrix medium to large organizations.
 Demonstrated experience in implementing contracting and procurement processes down to the end user level.
 Additional Requirements : 
 Experience in working with multi-disciplinary teams, contractors in a multicultural environment is an asset. 
 Communication/interpersonal skills – to be able to interact confidently with management and all hierarchical levels. 
 Self-starter, able to function effectively with minimal supervision.
 Accepts responsibility and demonstrates commitment to delivery of tasks and targets.
 Ability to be innovative and vision-oriented with ability to undertake both strategic planning and implementation.
 Ability to work well under pressure and handle multiple tasks and changing priorities within tight time frames.
 Ability to work collaboratively within a team environment.
 Energetic in pursuit of continuous improvement processes
 Shares knowledge readily and encourages personal development.
 As required, the position is based in Vancouver, BC, with the eventuality to relocate to Squamish (site). 
 Must be legally entitled to work in Canada. 
 Application Guidelines : 
 Only qualified candidates legally entitled to work in Canada will be contacted. 
 Thank you in advance for your interest!

About RIC Power Corp 
 RIC Power Corp. is owned by Panelmatic and designs and manufactures medium-voltage switchgear solutions for utilities, industrial facilities, and infrastructure projects where safety, reliability, and performance are critical. Our focus is on delivering engineered-to-order systems, including metal-enclosed, metal-clad, and arc-resistant switchgear, tailored to the unique requirements of each application. With a deep understanding of electrical distribution, protection, and safety standards, RIC Power develops solutions that support long-term system reliability while prioritizing operator safety and ease of maintenance. Every system is carefully engineered, manufactured, and assembled using proven components and industry-recognized practices to ensure consistent performance in demanding environments.
 The Mechanical Designer is responsible for the detailed design and 3D modeling of switchgear and power distribution products. Working under the technical guidance of the Mechanical Engineering Lead, this role transforms high-level concepts into manufacturing-ready drawing packages. The Designer ensures all outputs are accurate, feasible, and strictly adhere to RIC Power /Panelmatic design standards and Quality Management System (QMS).

 Create and maintain 3D models, parts, assemblies, and construction drawings using SolidWorks
 Generate accurate bills of materials (BOMs) to support manufacturing, procurement, and costing
 Work within established drawing standards, document control procedures, and PDM systems
 Maintain and update existing parts and assembly drawings, converting them into fabrication-ready drawings for production

 Participate in internal design reviews and contribute practical, production-focused solutions
 Collaborate closely with electrical designers and engineers to ensure proper mechanical–electrical integration
 Apply applicable codes and standards, including CSA, UL, IEEC, and internal company standards
 Ensure mechanical designs support regulatory compliance and safety requirements
 Work with the production team to develop assembly details, work instructions, and build sequences for complex assemblies
 review vendor drawings and technical documentation for accuracy and compatibility
 Interact with vendors and suppliers to integrate purchased components into designs
 Support engineering change processes (ECR/ECO) and maintain accurate revision control
 Assist with troubleshooting and resolving design-related issues during fabrication, assembly, and testing
 Provide informal technical guidance and knowledge sharing to junior designers as required.
 Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy 
 Strong proficiency with SolidWorks or a comparable 3D CAD platform
 Proven experience with sheet metal design and industrial enclosure fabrication
 Experience designing structural members, frames, and heavy-duty assemblies
 Solid understanding of manufacturing processes 
 Knowledge of tolerance stack-ups, fit, and function
 Ability to interpret electrical schematics and understand interface requirements
 Experience working within PDM/PLM systems (e.g., SolidWorks PDM)
 Proficiency with Microsoft Excel for BOMs, calculations, and engineering data tracking
 Strong communication, organization, and time-management skills
 Proactive problem-solving mindset with a focus on practical solutions
 Ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary team environment
 Asset: Experience with FEA analysis (static and/or dynamic) 
 Engineering degree or technical diploma (e.g., Mechanical Engineering, AScT)
 Eligibility or registration with Engineers and Geoscientists BC (EGBC) as a P.Eng. or EIT is an asset
 3- 5 years of experience in a mechanical and/or electrical manufacturing environment
 Demonstrated ability to produce mechanical general arrangement (GA) drawings and detailed part and assembly drawings
 Experience with large industrial equipment, custom-engineered products, or electrical enclosures
 Experience in medium voltage switchgear or power distribution equipment

About Owner

Owner is the AI-native system local business owners use to succeed, starting with restaurants.

We’re building the system that replaces the many tools owners use to run their business.

It powers everything from the restaurant’s website, online ordering, CRM, POS, and more.



Product philosophy

Most small business software makes owners do the work to get what they want: sales growth and profit growth. Owner does the work for them agentically.

Our system drives demand, converts it, and helps operators run their business day to day. As it improves, the business improves with it.

Using Owner should feel like having a team of great operators, engineers, and marketers working for you.



Our vision



We’re starting by helping independent restaurants succeed online.



But it’s not just restaurants that need our help. Most local businesses are struggling with these same problems. Huge technology corporations are taking their customers, bleeding their profits, and making it hard for them to survive.



Once we nail the solution for restaurants – we’ll scale it into every other local business type.



In the future we envision, tens of millions of local business owners will use our technology to succeed in the digital age.



Our traction



Since 2020, we've generated tens of millions in revenue and processed over a billion dollars of online orders. 1 in 5 Americans have used an Owner.com http://Owner.com website.



More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.



Our team



Our team is now in the low hundreds. We’ve got top talent from the most successful companies in SMB software, including: Shopify, HubSpot, DoorDash, ServiceTitan, Rappi, Faire and Stripe.



We’ll be scaling even faster in 2026 to keep pace with our customer growth.



Where we work



Owner is a remote-first, global company headquartered in San Francisco, with a sales hub in Toronto. For a few of our roles we prioritize in-person collaboration at one of our office locations. Most of our teammates are distributed throughout the globe. Please review the role description and discuss with your recruiter for more details on location!





Why we’re looking for you



Running a restaurant is a constant stream of decisions, exceptions, and tradeoffs. Most restaurant software gives operators more outputs: more dashboards, more alerts, more settings, more reports, and more things to check.




Owner is built around a different idea: software should help restaurants achieve outcomes. Our mobile and desktop experiences combine the essential tools operators need to run the business with the intelligence to tell them what matters, what to do next, and increasingly help do it for them.




We’re hiring a Principal Product Manager to own and scale this AI-native operator experience for restaurants. You’ll bring together the daily workflows operators rely on, from orders and guest issues to settings, performance, and growth opportunities. The goal is a cohesive product experience that turns signals into clear recommendations, simple actions, and trusted AI-assisted execution.




This is a hands-on, forward-deployed builder PM role for someone who wants to be close to the work: in restaurants, in kitchens, in text threads with operators, and alongside our frontline teams. You’ll pair that direct operator intuition with strong product taste and the technical judgment required to ship automation in messy, real-world workflows involving orders, menus, integrations, data quality, permissions, and reliability.




This role is 100% remote and can be based anywhere in the United States or Canada.



 The impact you'll have



 - Shift restaurant software from outputs to outcomes. Build experiences that synthesize what matters, explain why it matters, recommend the next best action, and make it easy to act.

 - Own the core operator experience across mobile and desktop. Bring together the workflows restaurants rely on every day, including orders, guest issues, operational settings, business performance, and growth opportunities, into a cohesive product experience.

 - Build personalized business guidance. Show restaurants the value Owner is driving, identify the highest-impact opportunities, and deliver the right recommendation across product, email, SMS, customer success, and AI agent experiences.

 - Scale unified guest and order management. Help restaurants monitor, manage, and resolve reviews, support requests, forms, order issues, and operational exceptions quickly.

 - Productize best-practice playbooks into simple actions. Turn proven operator and customer-success workflows into personalized recommendations, one-tap actions, and safe automation.

 - Earn trust in AI-assisted execution. Design the permissions, confirmations, evaluation loops, rollback paths, and failure handling needed for restaurants to trust Owner with increasingly important work.

 - Operate forward-deployed. Spend meaningful time with restaurant owners and teams — in restaurants, in kitchens, over text, and alongside our support and success teams — to understand what actually happens day to day. Turn that proximity into sharper product priorities, better AI behavior, and products that feel like real leverage for operators.

 - Lead through ambiguity. Align product, design, engineering, data, AI, customer success, and operations around the highest-impact operator outcomes.
   
   

 What we’re looking for



 - 8+ years of product management experience, or equivalent building experience, with a track record of shipping high-impact products.

 - Forward-deployed customer obsession. You build conviction by getting close to the work: visiting restaurants, observing live workflows, texting with operators, shadowing frontline teams, and understanding how work actually gets done before deciding what to build.

 - AI product instincts grounded in real operations. You think in loops — signals → decisions → actions → learning — and care deeply about quality, trust, and iteration.

 - Excellent product judgment and taste. You can reduce cognitive load, simplify messy workflows, and design products that feel obvious to busy, non-technical users.

 - Technical depth and strong engineering partnership. You can reason about systems, data flows, integrations, permissions, reliability, and tradeoffs.

 - Bias toward outcomes over features. You know how to connect product work to customer and business impact, not just launches.

 - Strong prioritization and execution. You can balance speed, correctness, and long-term maintainability in a fast-moving environment.

 - Cross-functional leadership. You can align opinionated stakeholders, create clarity from ambiguity, and keep teams moving.


Compensation and benefits



 - The estimated starting base salary range for this role is $280- $300K, plus a generous pre-IPO equity package

 - Other benefits include comprehensive health coverage, remote-first workplace, unlimited PTO - plus extra fun perks!





Notice - Employment Scams

Communication from our team regarding job opportunities will only be made by an Owner team member with an @owner.com email address.



We do not conduct interviews over email or chat platforms, and we will never ask you to provide personal or financial information such as your mailing address, social security number, credit card numbers or banking information. If you believe you are being contacted by a scammer, please mark the communication as "phishing" or “spam” and do not respond.

Does driving practical AI transformation for marketing teams get you excited?



Then Jobber might be the place for you! We’re looking for a AI Marketing Enablement Manager to join the Demand Generation team.

Jobber exists to help people in small businesses be successful. We work with small home service businesses, like your local plumbers, painters, and landscapers, to transform the way service is delivered through technology. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers, while providing an easy and professional customer experience. Running a small business today isn’t like it used to be—the way we consume and deliver service is changing rapidly, technology is evolving, and customers expect more. That’s why we put the power and flexibility in their hands to run their businesses how, where, and when they want!

Our culture of transparency, inclusivity, collaboration, and innovation has been recognized by Great Place to Work, Canada’s Most Admired Corporate Cultures, and more. Jobber has also been named on the Globe and Mail’s Canada’s Top Growing Companies list, and Deloitte Canada’s Technology Fast 50™, Enterprise Fast 15, and Technology Fast 500™ lists. With an Executive team that has over thirty years of industry experience of leading the way, we’ve come a long way from our first customer in 2011—but we’ve just scratched the surface of what we want to accomplish for our customers https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EkfZmHrRLx4&list=PLoktA_D-2UEnxMLfCe93bANKXVXd2bdN8&index=23.




THE TEAM

The Demand Generation team helps Jobber reach and engage small home service businesses through scalable marketing programs. We partner closely with Brand, Product Marketing, Marketing Operations, Sales, Data, and Product teams to create campaigns and experiences that drive awareness, pipeline, conversion, and customer growth.

This role will sit within Demand Generation and act as a force multiplier for the marketing organization. You’ll help marketers turn ideas into execution faster, reduce repetitive work, and develop new AI-enabled ways of planning, launching, analyzing, and optimizing campaigns.




THE ROLE

This is a builder-and-coach role and also an ownership role. You’ll inherit an in-flight AI enablement program, which is a library of tools, agents, MCP integrations, prompts, evals, documentation, and a partially enabled team. You’ll become the internal owner who extends it, keeps it reliable, and drives adoption across Demand Generation and adjacent marketing teams.

You’ll partner with marketers across campaign strategy, lifecycle, paid acquisition, SEO, GEO/AEO, content, CRO, marketing operations, and analytics. You’ll create practical solutions yourself, then help marketers adopt, adapt, and eventually build on them independently. Because this field moves fast, part of the job is keeping our approach current as models, tools, and best practices evolve. You’re defining a capability, not maintaining a fixed toolset.

And the ambition goes beyond doing today’s work faster. We want AI to expand what our marketing team can do at all. You will be surfacing opportunities we can’t currently see and taking on work that simply isn’t practical by hand, like analyzing every creative we’ve run to learn what truly drives performance. Efficiency is the floor; new capability is the ceiling. A core part of this role is finding those frontier use cases and turning the ones that prove valuable into things the team can rely on.




THE AI MARKETING ENABLEMENT MANAGER WILL:

 - Own the handover and the foundation
   
   - Take ownership of the assets built during our external engagement: tools, agents, MCP servers, prompts, evals, and documentation, and make sure they remain reliable, understood, and extensible after the vendor rolls off.
   
   - Own and advance the AI maturity model already in motion, moving marketers from first useful wins to regular integration to self-sufficiency, and reporting progress to leadership.
   
   - Own the marketing AI roadmap: prioritize what to build next, decide what to sunset, and set the standards and patterns the team builds against.

 - Build
   
   - Build AI-powered tools, agents, automations, and skills tailored to real marketing workflows - e.g. campaign planning, audience research, content development, channel execution, reporting, experimentation, and optimization.
   
   - Build and maintain integrations that connect AI to live data - e.g., MCP servers linking ad platforms, analytics, and CRM. This is so marketers can work against real data in natural language instead of exporting and reconciling by hand.
   
   - Establish quality and reliability practices: evals, regression tests, and human-in-the-loop review so tools can be trusted against real campaigns and real data, and so they don’t silently break when models or platforms change.

 - Expand what’s possible
   
   - Use AI to uncover opportunities the team can’t currently see: patterns across campaigns, audiences, creative, channels, and content that would be impractical to surface by hand.
   
   - Take on analysis at a scale humans can’t - e.g. evaluating hundreds of creative variants, ad transcripts, landing pages, or search terms at once to extract what’s working and why, then feeding that back into strategy.
   
   - Prototype net-new capabilities, not just faster versions of existing work: doing things we couldn’t do before, testing whether they hold, and turning the ones that prove valuable into durable, repeatable tools.

 - Coach and scale
   
   - Embed with marketers to deeply understand their workflows, goals, deliverables, tools, and pain points, and identify the highest-leverage places AI creates real leverage.
   
   - Coach marketers through a practical adoption journey, from first win to regular use to building their own workflows
   
   - Recognize patterns across individual use cases and turn one-offs into reusable playbooks, templates, and tools, documented in version control so any marketer can read, run, and extend them.
   
   - Share wins and examples to build momentum, confidence, and excitement around AI-enabled marketing work.
   
   - Extend the model beyond Demand Gen into the broader marketing organization as the capability matures.

 - Operate responsibly
   
   - Partner with Data, Security, and IT to keep solutions scalable, reliable, and responsible with approved AI providers, sound data handling, appropriate human review, and clear accountability for AI outputs and actions.
   
   - Track impact with the number of workflows transformed, time saved (measured before/after), adoption, maturity progression, and library reuse

 Internal applicants should apply with your work e-mail address . External applicants are considered only after the internal posting process has been completed. Only applicants chosen for an interview will be contacted. 
 SUMMARY OF DUTIES 
Reporting to a Supervisor, Hamilton Paramedic Service, the paramedic provides primary emergency medical care and transportation for ill and/or injured persons in the community to, from, and between treatment facilities, in specially equipped ambulance vehicles and emergency response vehicles. Paramedics also contribute to non-emergency and multi-disciplinary community care initiatives, through avenues such as public education, harm reduction, community paramedicine, palliative care, and other related programs.
 GENERAL DUTIES 
Provide primary emergency medical care for ill and/or injured persons at the emergency site by providing basic and advanced pre-hospital life support.
Provide transportation for ill and/or injured persons, to, from, and between treatment facilities, in specially equipped ambulance vehicles as directed by the dispatching Central Ambulance Communications Centre (CACC).
 Deliver thorough patient assessment and treatment in accordance to Provincial and local standards and medical directives.
Responsible for all medical interventions as deemed essential by the Base Hospital and Hamilton Paramedic Service, including: controlled drug therapy, manual defibrillation, and cardiac dysrhythmia interpretation according to Provincial Medical Directives.
Interact with members of the health care team, allied emergency care providers, the public, and patients in a professional manner.
Maintain communication with and follow the directions of all Central Ambulance Communication Centres (CACCs) encountered during operations, ensuring each CACC is kept informed of the paramedic’s status and location.
Assume a role of leadership, as required, and uphold patient advocacy.
Collaborate with medical personnel and allied emergency care providers to facilitate prompt treatment, support, and advocacy for the patients, their family and friends during the time of emergency care.
Participate in primary care, public health, public education, and community events as assigned.
Check, maintain, and stock fleet vehicles so-as to maintain the vehicle and vehicle equipment in a clean/sanitary, mechanically safe state of readiness in accordance with local and provincial standards.  Report any vehicle and/or equipment deficiencies and assist in corrective action where qualified.
Inspect, restock, and maintain ambulance stations in a clean and operational state.
Completion of all required documentation, including but not limited to Ambulance Call Reports, Incident/Occurrence Reports, Logistics Reports, Vehicle Inspection Reports, and any other report as deemed necessary by the Hamilton Paramedic Service and/or the Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care.
Participate in Continuing Education as required and participate in the training/precepting of Advanced Care and Primary Care paramedic students and other allied healthcare professionals.
Maintain all legislated requirements for employment and all certification requirements as set by the Base Hospital, the Hamilton Paramedic Service, and the MOHLTC.
Perform other duties, as assigned, which are directly related to the major responsibilities of the job.
 QUALIFICATIONS 
1. Must hold certification as a Primary Care Paramedic or higher or be eligible for certification prior to start of employment.
 2. Diploma or letter confirming good standing and indicating program completion date from an approved Ontario Primary Care Paramedic (PCP) Training Program required prior to hiring.
 3. If graduation was prior to 2003, must provide proof of completion of all mandatory Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care core programs via individual certificates or with a letter attesting to completion by an approved Ontario PCP Training Program.
 4. Current Basic Life Support (BLS) Provider certificate or CPR Healthcare Provider (HCP) certificate or Advanced Cardiac Life Support (ACLS) certificate.
 5. Hold the qualification of, or have obtained a pass standing, in an advanced emergency medical care assistant examination (AEMCA), or equivalent, as outlined in the Ambulance Act O. Reg. 257/00.
 6. If non-AEMCA certified, must have successfully completed an approved Ontario PCP Training Program and must achieve AEMCA Certification within 210 days of paramedic program completion as per Ministry of Health and Long-Term Care guidelines, unless otherwise specified by the MOHLTC (per Ambulance Act Reg. 257/00).
 7. Must possess and maintain a valid Ontario Driver's Licence that authorizes the operation and driving of an ambulance.
 8. Must meet all current requirements (including medical) of the Ambulance Act and Regulations, including the current Ambulance Service Communicable Disease Standards. As a condition of employment, you will be required to provide proof of the minimum requirements required as outlined in the Ambulance Act and Regulations.
 9. Must successfully complete any/all requirements and become fully certified by the Centre for Paramedic Education and Research (CPER) with Hamilton Health Sciences (HHS) Base Hospital Program (including, but not limited to, palliative care certification within the first 6 months of certification).
 10. Demonstrated ability to read, write, and speak English proficiently.
 11. Proven ability to demonstrate leadership and take command during emergency situations.
 12. Must be in good physical health and capable of lifting heavy weights.
 13. Proven ability to exercise sound judgement in emergency situations.
 14. You must acknowledge and agree to comply with any future vaccine policy requirements as an ongoing condition of employment at the City of Hamilton.
 15. Preference may be given to those with additional relevant education (e.g. ACLS/PALS/ITLS/NRP/PEARS certification), experience, and/or related employment (paramedic, medical transfer, and other allied health professions). The Senior Planner provides integrated project planning leadership across the full project lifecycle for nuclear power projects. The role develops the project's planning framework — WBS, execution strategies, milestone logic, progress measurement systems, and integrated baselines — ensuring that scope, schedule, cost, and resources are planned coherently and that the project can measure, forecast, and control performance from contract award through to handover.

  Establish the project planning framework: WBS, control accounts, milestone hierarchy, planning procedures, and the project execution plan (PEP) planning inputs.
 Develop integrated plans combining schedule, cost, resources, risk, and procurement strategy into a single project baseline.

Gestionnaire Fiscal 
Le ou la gestionnaire fiscal(e) au sein du département des finances de Mistplay jouera un rôle clé dans la mise en œuvre de notre stratégie fiscale mondiale, la gestion de nos obligations de conformité fiscale et la défense lors des vérifications fiscales. Cette personne sera également responsable de la gestion de notre registre des risques fiscaux et veillera au respect des obligations fiscales internationales dans l’ensemble de nos territoires d’activités.
Relevant du contrôleur, directeur de la comptabilité, vous agirez comme principal point de liaison entre Mistplay et nos conseillers fiscaux externes. Vous aurez pour mandat d’atténuer les risques fiscaux et de soutenir la croissance stratégique de l’entreprise. Il s’agit d’une occasion hautement interfonctionnelle qui s’adresse à une personne qui aime collaborer étroitement avec les équipes des affaires juridiques, des finances et les conseillers externes.
Ce que vous ferez chez Mistplay
- Diriger les stratégies de défense lors des vérifications menées par l’Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) et Revenu Québec (RQ), notamment en ce qui concerne les dispositions relatives aux programmes de fidélisation, l’impôt sur le revenu des sociétés et les nouvelles cotisations de taxes à la consommation, en collaboration avec les équipes des affaires juridiques et des finances.
- Tenir à jour le calendrier centralisé de conformité fiscale et le registre de suivi des défenses lors des vérifications, en assurant la gestion des avis légaux, des processus d’opposition et des délais de nouvelle cotisation pour les années prescrites.
- Piloter la stratégie en matière de prix de transfert et finaliser les ententes intersociétés afin d’atténuer les risques liés à l’existence d’un établissement stable dans différents territoires, notamment en Italie, au Japon et en Ontario, tout en supervisant la documentation annuelle des prix de transfert.
- Diriger les stratégies de migration des contrats internationaux, notamment le transfert des ententes avec les éditeurs et les annonceurs entre les différentes entités de Mistplay, afin d’assurer leur harmonisation avec la structure fiscale mondiale de l’entreprise.
- Superviser la conformité fiscale transfrontalière, notamment les obligations de déclaration fiscales fédérales et étatiques aux États-Unis, la paie multiétatique, le suivi du lien fiscal (sales tax nexus) et les mécanismes de paie miroir (shadow payroll) pour les employés en Italie, à Chypre et de part et d’autre de la frontière canado-américaine.
- Gérer les obligations fiscales liées à l’emploi, notamment l’impôt-santé des employeurs de l’Ontario (EHT) et les retenues à la source applicables à l’exercice d’options d’achat d’actions au Canada.
- Diriger la préparation et la soumission des demandes de crédits et d’incitatifs fiscaux de Mistplay, notamment les demandes fédérales et provinciales de crédits pour la RS&DE, le crédit d’impôt C3i du Québec et les obligations de conformité liées au programme IRAP, en collaboration avec nos conseillers fiscaux externes.
- Préparer et produire les déclarations mensuelles de taxes à la consommation, ainsi que gérer la production des déclarations annuelles d’impôt sur le revenu des sociétés.

Titre de CPA ou diplôme d’études supérieures équivalent en fiscalité ou en comptabilité.
Expérience significative en gestion de la conformité fiscale des sociétés au Canada et à l’international, notamment en matière de vérifications de l’ARC et de Revenu Québec, ainsi que de programmes d’incitatifs fiscaux RS&DE et C3i.
Excellente connaissance des règles internationales en matière de prix de transfert, des risques liés aux établissements stables et du suivi du lien fiscal (tax nexus) dans les différents États américains.
Connaissance des incidences fiscales liées à la rémunération en actions, notamment les évaluations 409A et les retenues à la source mondiales applicables aux options d’achat d’actions.
Expérience éprouvée dans la gestion de conseillers fiscaux externes de premier plan et de conseillers juridiques, ainsi que dans l’établissement de collaborations efficaces avec ces derniers.
